purpose: The ONLY place this repository may record that a vendored Cortex product gate or work package (v0.15 or v0.22) has moved off its shipped, honest default. scripts/cortex_package_gate.sh (v0.15) and scripts/cortex_package_gate_v022.sh (v0.22) both run scripts/cortex_honesty_invariant.py, which fails if a vendored gate_manifest.json claims a product_result other than NOT_RUN, or task_manifest.json a status other than 'Not started', without a matching row here that names a file in THIS repo which actually runs and is actually invoked. Every row is re-validated by both gates on every run.
how_to_add_a_row: 1. Implement the gate for real as a repo-owned script or test (e.g. scripts/cx02_observation_gate.sh). It must exit non-zero when the property it checks is false.

2. Wire it into an invoker that actually runs -- normally scripts/gate.sh. scripts/cortex_honesty_invariant.py greps the invoker for the executed_by path, so a row naming a script nothing calls is REJECTED. That is what stops this file becoming a rubber stamp.

3. Add a row below with gate_id, executed_by (repo-relative), invoked_by (repo-relative), allowed_product_result and a note saying what is measured. Every row is re-validated on every gate run, including rows for gates the package still reports as NOT_RUN -- a row whose script is deleted or unwired breaks the day it rots, not the day someone flips a manifest.

4. Do NOT edit the vendored gate_manifest.json. Two independent things forbid it: the package's own tools/validate_package.py hard-fails on any product_result other than NOT_RUN ('package must not claim a product run'), and SHA256SUMS_v0_15.json / SHA256SUMS_v0_22.json pin the file. NOT_RUN is a true statement about the PACKAGE -- 'this package does not execute it' -- and stays true no matter what this repository implements. This registry, not the vendored manifest, is where this repository records that it runs a gate.

5. If a future upstream release re-vendors the package WITH results filled in, the honesty check will accept a non-NOT_RUN product_result only for gates that have a valid row here, and only when the result is in allowed_product_result.
Removing a gate's implementation means removing its row.

B271. Branches from one frozen published base, each with its own run id/writer, budgets carved inside one regime (Journal::reserve_within). axon-fabric/tests/branches.rs. No CLI verb yet.

B271. Publish requires expected head, current epoch, branch writer, a passing receipt from this journal/branch binding the exact version, and a declared approver who is not the writer; concurrent publishers: exactly one wins. Approvers/writers are declared names, not signatures. axon-fabric/tests/branches.rs.
B271. Cancelling a branch keeps every record and any liability and leaves sibling branches untouched. axon-fabric/tests/branches.rs.

B280. REAL process deaths (abort() in a crash child at SubmitConfig.fault_hook boundaries; SIGKILL of the real axon-fabric CLI) at every submit effect boundary — after intent, after reserve, after the launch record, after the terminal record — plus inside branch cancellation and inside an axon-loop pointer transition (after the ledger append, after the projection; axon_loop::ledger::set_fault_hook). A restart resumes a pre-launch orphan exactly once (never under a superseded epoch; released in a cancelled branch), keeps a launched op OutcomeUnknown with its liability and never re-runs it, and the check worker dies with its supervisor (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG). Tests: axon-fabric restart_matrix.rs, submit.rs, journal.rs; axon-loop pointer.rs. NOT covered by a real kill: the Linux microVM profile (its launcher path is BLOCKED on the operator-signed B263 qualification).

B280. Authority-peer outage at submit and between submit and dispatch (an absent store is refused, not read as epoch 0 — FG-048), a re-send after reconnect through the library and the real CLI (one run, budget committed once), authority that moved while away (new request refused, recorded answer kept), another schema version or an unknown field refused before the journal, a partial export refused then the complete one recorded once (a partial re-send is not a replay), an episode of another schema version refused, and a replayed activation after a later pause that re-activates nothing. Tests: axon-fabric peer_failure_matrix.rs; axon-loop intake.rs, pointer.rs. The MiCode-side peer failures (old/absent adapter, no common profile, fabricated accept, Fabric refusal) are loop_interop_gate.sh sections 8-9 and MiCode's own tests.

B282. Attacks on Fabric's routes into authority, on the selected profile (process_scoped/local-interpreter): a repository shipping its own check/grant registries (refused; its executable never runs), re-attaching a different outcome to a finished op or attaching one to an unfinished op (refused before any write; replays keep the original receipt), argv escaping the workspace, the legacy single-file fallback's live-file swap (no verdict on bytes it did not judge), per-trial cache isolation, grant authority (grant_authority.rs: grant_ref bound to its principal, pinned grant files) and check effects (check_effects.rs: hidden suite, substituted suite/executable/argv, stale epoch). Verifier separation is G32 below. NOT covered: the Linux microVM profile (BLOCKED on the operator-signed B263 qualification) and settlement, which is library-only accounting, not an admission route.

B282. Each laundering class — mutated receipt, forged issuer identity, hash-only success, missing attempt, cross-tenant reference — on individually schema-valid documents with re-derived digests, driven through independent evaluation -> admission -> the fenced pointer: never a verified pass, never Accepted, pointer never moves, each refused by its own first-line check (mutation-proven), with a clean positive control Accepted (axon-loop evidence_laundering.rs). Intake step 8 refuses laundered Fabric verification evidence (intake.rs).

B260. Intent durable before begin returns; a real crash at each submit boundary (after intent, reserve, launch record, terminal) recovers exactly one recorded op with no blind re-execution; the same OperationId with changed input is a conflict with zero effects; the journal survives restart (torn tail truncated, state visible after reopen). axon-fabric journal.rs, submit.rs, restart_matrix.rs.

B274 mechanism. Too little evidence, liability, unknowns, regression or no economic benefit gives Inconclusive/Reject, never a forced winner (zero-pass and zero-vs-zero never Accepted); thresholds cannot change after outcomes (freeze is permanent, plan shopping refused, trials before freeze refused). axon-loop evl_admission.rs, redteam.rs. The PILOT's own frozen values are Stage 7.

B278 mechanism. Activation checks the expected active policy, the monotonic epoch fence, the exact admitted candidate (activating anything but the admitted policy, or under an unknown admission, is refused), the candidate list and revocation immediately before publication; concurrent activations (threads and two real CLI processes) have exactly one winner; a replayed or stale activation never overwrites. Every refusal writes zero bytes. axon-loop pointer.rs, candidates.rs, cli.rs.

B260. A check that times out after its launch record gives receipt TimedOut / verification Unknown, projected to episode OutcomeUnknown, with its whole reservation kept as outstanding liability (neither refunded nor charged as known); a re-send with the same operation id replays that answer and never re-runs it (the worker is started exactly once). A launched op whose supervisor dies (SIGKILL, abort) is OutcomeUnknown with liability kept and never re-run; unknown billing keeps the full reservation; an unknown outcome can be settled with evidence but never marked completed. axon-fabric submit.rs, journal.rs, restart_matrix.rs.

B286. governance/v022_release_claims.json holds engineering_qualified, policy_activated and measured_improvement_supported as three separate fields; each may be true only with evidence of its own kind (a release-verified receipt; an admission plus its activation transition; a measured-claim report with population and uncertainty), one claim's evidence never stands for another's, no merged field is allowed, and absence leaves a claim false. All three are false today (no pilot, not release-verified). The validator self-tests the cases it must refuse before reading the record.

B272. No speculative-effect path exists, and a request cannot ask for one: marking work speculative, pre-dispatching alternatives or naming a second dispatch authority is refused by the closed request schema before the journal (nothing journalled, nothing spawned). An approved branch (B271) keeps exact selected bytes (publication requires the exact verified output), shared cost (every branch carves within one declared regime) and cancellation semantics (a cancelled branch keeps its record and liability) rather than becoming an alternate dispatch authority. axon-fabric joint_bypass.rs, branches.rs.

B257. Repeated trials of one task and arm are distinct and all execute (Fabric) and are all recorded (axon-loop intake) — the same task id never deduplicates a fresh trial; only a transport retry (identical OperationId and input) replays; an authorized new execution of a trial carries a new AttemptId and op and runs; reusing an OperationId for other input is a conflict; the same trial with different bytes is a conflict; trial ids are never reused across experiments. axon-fabric submit.rs; axon-loop intake.rs, redteam.rs.

B273. The EVO proposer changes only the shortlist: its candidate records the parent policy and its discovery evidence, keeps the candidate set and controls (model/evaluator route) byte-equal, never sets authority_expansion, never adds an id, and its hypothesis history is append-only; a tool-adding or widening candidate is refused at put, at freeze and at activation; the frozen plan (evaluator, promotion rule, task corpus) is permanent and plan shopping is refused. The proposer emits data only and has no route to code or permissions. axon-loop plan_evo_tel.rs, candidates.rs, redteam.rs.

B276. A pass needs nonzero applicable checks: verification 'passed' with zero matched checks is invalid in the contract, a real interpreter run that exits 0 matching nothing is NotRun, and a named check that is absent is NotRun with 0 matched. Over exact candidate bytes: output changed after verification is never a pass. No offsetting: one failed check fails a whole suite whatever the rest scored, exit code zero never stands for a verdict, and low cost never offsets inferior quality at admission. axon-fabric submit.rs; axon-cortex check_executor.rs; axon-loop-contracts fixtures.rs; axon-loop evl.rs, evl_admission.rs.

B267. Section 10 of the paired interop gate, real binaries both sides: a pinned MiCode task reads Axon's REAL `axon-loop pointer show` output at every tool execution. While the pinned policy is in force its `read` runs; after a REAL `axon-loop pointer revoke` the same task still starts (the pin agreed at task start) but the `read` is refused at execution and its content never reaches the model. Discriminates: against MiCode 29446ec9 (pre-fix) exactly the two revoked assertions fail. MiCode side (micode c1bc363c): the fence is checked before the gate AND immediately before execute (a revocation during an approval wait still stops the effect), refuses when the view cannot vouch (unreadable, other scope, older epoch), is inherited by children (derive_spec) and required at spawn (child_is_within); the shortlist is the enforced tool_allowlist so candidate identity holds in children; retries are new dispatched calls and rechecked. Tests: micode-core dispatch::tests::{a_revoked_pinned_policy_stops_the_next_call_and_every_retry, an_authority_view_that_cannot_vouch_for_the_pin_refuses_the_call, a_revocation_during_an_approval_wait_stops_the_effect}, scope::tests::a_child_must_carry_its_parents_authority_fence_unchanged, micode-delegate task_tool::tests::a_child_inherits_its_parents_authority_fence, micode closed_loop_v022_real_binary::a_revoked_policy_is_refused_at_tool_execution_through_the_real_binary (run by the Stage-5 micode-suite harness).

B267. Real binaries: loop_interop_gate section 5 — a policy naming a tool outside the registered candidate list is refused by Axon policy put (exit 4, naming the tool, store unchanged) and, fed to MiCode anyway, abstains to the incumbent with zero tool additions (the added tool never reaches the provider). MiCode (09717d17): a shortlist must be a subset of the session's authorized candidates and bound to their cl22 view (active_policy::tests::invalid_policies_abstain_to_the_incumbent_with_a_reason); the shortlist is the enforced, INHERITED tool allowlist, so a delegated child whose dispatch is rebuilt from the full registry is still refused a tool the policy did not shortlist (closed_loop_v022_real_binary::a_delegated_child_is_held_to_the_policys_shortlist_through_the_real_binary, mutation-checked); concrete file effects are checked against inherited path/write scopes and a child must be provably within its parent (scope::tests::{path_globs_cover_exact_paths_and_directory_prefixes_only, the_write_set_bounds_writes_but_not_reads, a_child_must_be_provably_within_its_parent}); an unknown glob/subset relation is denied, never assumed narrower (scope::tests::an_unprovable_pattern_fails_closed_everywhere).

B268. Real binaries: loop_interop_gate sections 3 and 5 — Axon's DEC policy narrows MiCode's sent tool set to exactly its shortlist, and a tool-adding policy is refused at put and abstains in MiCode with zero additions. A policy can do nothing but reorder/narrow: Axon refuses at put, naming the field, a policy that ALSO names a tool list, permission, verifier, model, compute profile, credential route, budget or skill (axon-loop tests/cli.rs a_policy_that_names_any_other_authority_dimension_is_refused_at_put — two independent layers, schema additionalProperties:false and serde deny_unknown_fields; dropping both lets it through, measured), and MiCode abstains on the same documents naming the field (active_policy::tests::a_policy_naming_any_other_authority_dimension_abstains_naming_it, mutation-checked). authority_expansion:true is refused on both sides. Skills are not policy-selectable at all: the candidate view is the tool registry.

B266, third use site. Named MiCode tests, run by exact name against the paired MiCode revision: every result a child of a closed-loop task returns is classified against the parent's CURRENT context before the parent sees it — the parent's current integration head (re-observed at intake, not the launch head), its current declaration (model route, build namespace, whether it still declares a context at all) and its declared write set. Stale worker success is directly_integratable / needs_rebase / conflicting / obsolete, obsolete outranking conflicting, and the class rides the result as a runtime footer the child cannot author, plus a written receipt; a receipt that cannot be produced renders as 'integrability unknown; do not merge', never as integratable. MiCode never merges a child's work, so nothing is admitted against a different base. result_receipt::tests::a_result_is_classified_against_the_parents_current_context (every class and every obsolete condition); assembly::tests::v022_a_returned_result_is_classified_against_the_parents_current_context (the production driver, real git: own work / parent landed a commit / write outside the set / parent rewound — mutations recorded in the test).

B256. BOTH REAL PEERS, real binaries, before any model call or dispatch (loop_interop_gate.sh): section 5 feeds each malformed policy document to real `axon-loop policy put` (refused, store unchanged) and to real `micode exec` (abstains, zero tool additions, the incumbent's single provider request) — duplicate key; ESCAPED-ALIAS key (`controls\u005fref`, each peer names the DECODED duplicate `controls_ref`, proving it decoded the escape); unknown closed field; malformed digest; tool-adding shortlist; authority_expansion. Unsafe numbers where each peer reads numbers: 2^53+1 as MiCode's expected-context authority_epoch (refused before any provider request) and as Axon's pointer-transition expected_epoch (exit 3, store unchanged). Incompatible required capabilities: section 9, the real cortex-policy-adapter and real MiCode with no common closed-loop profile — explicit unsupported, persisted, zero model calls, distinct from an old peer. Syntactic fixtures alone are not claimed: every case above crosses a real process boundary.

B256. Old peer / absent peer (loop_interop_gate.sh sections 0 and 9): MiCode with no expected context runs as the incumbent and writes no closed-loop artefact; the real adapter and MiCode negotiate closed-loop-profile/1 with every outcome persisted before the first model call — agreed, old peer (explicit, retained-authority incumbent), no common profile (explicit unsupported), fabricated accept (recorded failed). Old episodes remain readable through PINNED adapters, never reinterpreted: MiCode's canonical episode spend (micode 7070c8ca) — v014 episodes carry a never-written micro_cents 0 which the in-place G1 change had read as a KNOWN ZERO (every historical episode free); spend is now appended as spend_micro_cents and one pinned table on both peers reads v014 0 as unknown (MiCode episode::tests::every_historical_spend_shape_reads_without_reinterpretation over a whole v014 episode; Axon intake::every_historical_spend_shape_is_read_through_the_pinned_table), and the real join refuses a v014-shaped canonical episode against a metered sidecar BY THE COST JOIN (section 4; discriminates vs micode 09717d17). Axon's own Cortex episode format and digest rule are pinned unchanged since the v0.22 base (axon-cortex conformance::a_pre_v022_episode_reads_and_keeps_its_digest). Axon-side negotiation vectors: v022_stage5_gates.sh (axon-loop-contracts profile, cortex-policy-adapter negotiate).

tasks_note: A work package status other than 'Not started' needs a row in `tasks` with task_id and allowed_status. A status in {Done, Complete, Completed, Landed} additionally requires every one of that task's gate_targets to have a valid row in `gates` -- so 'Done' cannot launder an unexecuted gate.
